t.6.37.1: When the son of Rāvaṇa, having achieved his purpose, had gone back into Laṅkā, the bull-like leaders of the monkeys, stricken with distress, surrounded Rāghava and guarded him.
t.6.37.2: Hanumān, Aṅgada, Nīla, Suṣeṇa, Kumuda, and Nala, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, and Gandhamādana.
t.6.37.3: Jāmbavān, Ṛṣabha, Sunda, Rambha, Śatabali and Pṛthu, their ranks drawn up in battle array and ever vigilant, took up trees from every side.
t.6.37.4: Gazing in all directions, sideways and upward, the monkeys thought, "They are rākṣasas!" even when mere blades of grass stirred.
t.6.37.5: Rāvaṇa too, greatly delighted, having dismissed his son Indrajit, then summoned the rākṣasī women who were guarding Sītā.
t.6.37.6: The rākṣasīs, and Trijaṭā too, presented themselves before him at his command. Then the delighted lord of the rākṣasas spoke to those rākṣasīs.
t.6.37.7: Announce to Vaidehī that Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa have been slain by Indrajit, and, having made her mount the Puṣpaka, show her the two lying slain on the battlefield.
t.6.37.8: Her husband, relying on whom she has stood firm and does not come to me, has been struck down together with his brother at the forefront of battle.
t.6.37.9: Free from doubt, untroubled and without longing, Maithilī Sītā, adorned with all her ornaments, will come to me.
t.6.37.11: Having heard those words of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, the rākṣasīs said, "So be it," and went to where the Puṣpaka was.
t.6.37.10: Today, seeing Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa fallen in battle under the sway of Time, she, her hope turned away, will see no other refuge.
t.6.37.12: Then, at Rāvaṇa's command, the rākṣasīs took the Puṣpaka and brought to it Maithilī, who was staying in the Aśoka grove.
t.6.37.13: Then the rākṣasīs took Sītā, who was wholly overcome by grief for her husband, and placed her upon the aerial chariot Puṣpaka.
t.6.37.14: Then, having placed Sītā together with Trijaṭā upon the Puṣpaka, Rāvaṇa had Laṅkā adorned with garlands of banners and flags.
t.6.37.15: And the lord of the Rākṣasas, overjoyed, had it proclaimed throughout Laṅkā: "Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa have both been slain in battle by Indrajit!"
t.6.37.16: Sītā, having gone in the aerial chariot together with Trijaṭā, saw the entire army of the Vānaras struck down.
t.6.37.18: Then Sītā saw them both, Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma, lying on beds of arrows, unconscious and tormented by the arrows.
t.6.37.17: She saw the flesh-eaters with delighted hearts, and she also saw the monkeys, stricken with grief, at the side of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.37.20: Seeing there those two heroic brothers, bulls among men, Sītā, exceedingly afflicted with grief, lamented piteously.
t.6.37.21: Stricken by tears and grief, she gazed upon those two brothers, whose might was equal to that of the gods, and, believing them dead, she, overwhelmed with sorrow, spoke these words.
t.6.37.19: The two heroes, their armor shattered and their bows flung away, every limb torn by arrows, lying on the ground as though turned into thickets of arrows.
